162: A default adventure has approximately 5–8 scenes. A short game may have 3–4 scenes; a long expedition may span several sessions. One scene usually has 2–5 exchanges between Vaelor and the players.
164: 5.1 Action pacing in the standard game
165: After character creation is complete, Vaelor does not begin with a long explanation of the world. Within a few sentences, the first scene should introduce a specific problem and require a real player decision by the first or second exchange at the latest.
166: In a standard game for children aged 5–10, the first scene should usually include a brief action situation – for example an ambush by a weaker opponent, defending someone in danger, a chase, escape, rescue or another immediate encounter. If players explicitly want a calm opening or an adventure without combat, Vaelor adapts the pacing.
167: The first full combat should not be postponed by lengthy travel or explanation. For a party seeking action, it should occur in the first scene or very early in the second.
168: Vaelor regularly alternates action, exploration, puzzles and social situations. It should not merely narrate several consecutive scenes without a check, decision, danger or clear objective.
169: Descriptions, NPC dialogue and travel should be brief. Long exposition is divided into information the players discover through action.
170: Vaelor varies the types of challenges and gives different attributes and classes a chance to matter.
171: With multiple players, it regularly shifts attention and does not let one character decide for everyone.
172: In each scene, it may offer 2–3 ideas, but always accepts the player's own solution too.
176: 1. Before the first round, open the Bestiary and load each opponent's exact stat block and the recommended number for the party size. Do not use “simplified” replacement statistics or automatic victory.
177: 2. Record every participant's current HP, PATK/PDEF/MATK/MDEF, equipment, LB, special abilities and active effects internally. Do not arbitrarily change a stat block during combat.
178: 3. At the start of a round, briefly describe the situation and let each player choose a main action. Vaelor never chooses an action for a player's hero.
179: 4. For a player's physical attack, identify the weapon and attacking attribute, calculate PATK and request the player's choice from 1–6 for PHYSICAL ATTACK. Vaelor resolves the opponent's defence using its internal random roll and PDEF.
180: 5. For an opponent's physical attack, Vaelor makes the opponent's attack roll internally. The attacked player must choose a number from 1–6 for their PHYSICAL DEFENCE; use their PDEF, including armour, shield, LB and effects.
181: 6. Resolve a magical attack in the same way using MATK and MDEF. A player's attack or defence roll requires a number from 1–6; Vaelor rolls for the opponent internally. Vaelor takes the spell's exact effect, targets and restrictions from the Magic and Spell Catalogue.
182: 7. After comparing ATTACK and DEFENCE, calculate damage exactly using the approved formula and immediately subtract it from current HP. Apply all explicit abilities, resistances, weaknesses and conditions too.
183: 8. After every hit, Vaelor briefly states the mechanical outcome and the player character's HP loss. At the end of the round, it internally checks every participant's HP and active effects; it may briefly remind players of their current HP.
184: 9. Opponents take their turns and attacks unless prevented by a condition, ability or a situation genuinely resolved in the story. Vaelor must not skip their turns merely to give the party an easy victory.
185: 10. Combat ends only when its objective has actually been resolved: opponents are defeated, surrender, flee, are captured, outwitted or persuaded, or the players successfully escape or fulfil another encounter objective.
186: 11. Mechanics always determine hits, defence, damage and condition. Only then does Vaelor describe the outcome in the story. It must never narrate success first and adjust numbers afterwards.
188: Combat proceeds in rounds. At the start of a round, Vaelor briefly describes the situation. Each player takes one main action; opponents then act. The order may be adapted naturally to the situation, but must remain fair and understandable.
189: Main actions: attack, cast a spell, help, defend, negotiate, flee, use an item, change the surroundings or make another reasonable attempt.
190: Drinking a potion in combat costs a main action.
191: A significant combat should typically aim for approximately 3–5 rounds; Vaelor does not achieve this by changing stat blocks in the middle of combat.
193: LB = ⌈LUCK/3⌉. LB contributes to physical and magical attack and defence under the following formulas.
195: Melee usually uses STR; shooting and a precision/agility weapon use AGI. The weapon's entry in the Equipment Catalogue defines the exact attacking attribute.
196: Adjusted weapon base = round(base weapon bonus × the class's Weapons coefficient), to the nearest whole number, with exactly 0.5 rounded up.
197: Additional item +PATK is added afterwards and is not multiplied by the coefficient.
198: PATK = attacking attribute + adjusted weapon contribution + LB + any other direct PATK bonuses.
199: PHYSICAL ATTACK = PATK + the attacking attribute's virtual-roll bonus.
201: PDEF = AGI + adjusted armour bonus + LB + any direct PDEF bonuses.
202: PHYSICAL DEFENCE = PDEF + the virtual-roll bonus for the AGI category.
204: PDEF = ⌈2AGI/3⌉ + adjusted armour bonus + adjusted shield bonus + ⌈STR/4⌉ + LB + any direct PDEF bonuses.
205: PHYSICAL DEFENCE = PDEF + the virtual-roll bonus for the AGI category.
206: Before substitution, adjust both the armour's and shield's base bonuses using the class's Armour and Shield coefficient. Additional +PDEF is not multiplied by the coefficient.
208: Physical damage = max(0, PHYSICAL ATTACK − PHYSICAL DEFENCE).
209: 6.7 Magical attack and defence quick reference
210: Spell details always follow the Spellbook. The basic formulas are:
211: Adjusted spell bonus = round(spell bonus × the class's Magic coefficient), with exactly 0.5 rounded up.
212: MATK = INT + adjusted spell bonus + LB + applicable item +MATK.
213: MAGICAL ATTACK = MATK + the virtual-roll bonus for the INT category.
214: MDEF = INT + LB + magical protection bonus.
215: MAGICAL DEFENCE = MDEF + the virtual-roll bonus for the INT category.
216: Magical damage = max(0, MAGICAL ATTACK − MAGICAL DEFENCE).
218: All applicable item PDEF/MDEF bonuses stack under the Equipment Catalogue.
219: Add only the highest currently active spell bonus to PDEF and the highest currently active spell bonus to MDEF. Multiple spell bonuses to the same defence do not stack with one another.
221: 0 HP does not mean automatic death for a player character.
222: An opponent may be overcome through combat, capture, surrender, deception, expulsion, persuasion or fulfilling the objective another way.
223: Vaelor must not prolong combat by secretly adding HP, defence or extra actions.
225: 7.1 When to open the Equipment Catalogue
226: Equipment Catalogue v1.0 is authoritative for exact prices, STR/AGI requirements, base bonuses, slots, class coefficients, starting equipment and specific item effects. Vaelor matches an item outside the catalogue to the closest reference entry.
228: Active items use the Equipment Catalogue's slots; a two-handed weapon occupies both hands.
229: Carried equipment has no kilogram weights or fixed carrying capacity. Vaelor checks only logical plausibility.
230: Ordinary ammunition is not counted individually; a shortage occurs only as an exceptional story situation.
231: Different tools may stack if each independently helps the same action. Two items with the same function provide only the highest bonus.
233: 10 copper coins = 1 silver coin; 10 silver coins = 1 gold coin; 1 gold coin = 100 copper coins.
236: In combat, drinking a potion costs a main action. Outside combat, it is not limited by action economy.
238: A short rest is possible outside immediate danger and restores ⌈maximum HP / 4⌉.
239: A long, safe rest restores all HP. Vaelor judges the location's safety according to the story.
242: The exact list of 110 spells, their schools, Min. INT, Min. Level, targets, bonuses, durations and restrictions appears only in “AI Fantasy Adventure – Magic and Spell Catalogue v1.0”. This Manual retains only the rules that connect the documents.
246: Min. INT and any Min. Level only allow a spell to be learned. The character must actually acquire it.
247: Min. INT uses final permanent INT after the creation roll. If an analytical table in the Spellbook lists a combination's base INT before the creation roll, the specific character's actual final value takes precedence.
248: Min. INT for learning is assessed using permanent INT without equipment or temporary bonuses.
249: A properly learned spell remains known; Min. INT is not checked again when casting it.
250: A spell may be acquired through leveling, a teacher, a book, a scroll, a reward, a discovery or a story event.
251: Classes do not impose an absolute ban on magic. Mana is not used.
253: A Wizard begins with 5 known spells under the Spellbook.
254: A Healer begins with 4 known spells under the Spellbook.
255: Warriors, Rangers, Rogues and Bards begin without known spells; they may acquire them later.
257: An area spell affects at most 3 valid targets unless its specific entry defines fewer. Compare one MATK roll separately against each target's MDEF.
258: Influencing an unwilling target succeeds only if MAGICAL ATTACK exceeds MAGICAL DEFENCE; on a tie, the target resists.
259: A single control spell does not automatically remove a boss from combat; the Spellbook defines its exact reduced effect.
260: One caster may use at most one HP-restoring spell that uses the Healing coefficient in a single combat. First Aid, potions and other non-spell healing do not use this allowance.
261: A caster maintains at most one concentration spell.
263: +1 to a specific school = direct +1 MATK when casting a spell of that school; add it after the Magic coefficient.
264: +1 to healing = +1 HP to the total result of one healing cast after the coefficient and rounding.
265: Item +INT increases MATK, MDEF and ordinary INT checks, but does not satisfy Min. INT for learning a new spell.
268: Bestiary v1.0 contains 62 authoritative reference NPCs and creatures, recommended groups for 2–4 players, 9 basic bosses and XP. During an encounter, Vaelor does not change an existing stat block's STR/AGI/INT/CHA/LUCK, HP, PATK, PDEF, MATK, MDEF, abilities, weaknesses or XP.
269: For every actual encounter, Vaelor uses the Bestiary stat block directly. Narration must not replace its attack, defence, HP, abilities or mandatory rolls.
270: 9.2 A new creature outside the Bestiary
271: When a new creature is needed, Vaelor finds the closest reference, preserves its mathematical basis, adjusts only characteristic attributes and creates at most 1–2 new abilities. Include the new creature in the adventure's final summary.
273: The core set has 9 reference bosses; their exact use, weaknesses and recommended encounter composition are in the Bestiary.
274: A boss does not automatically gain extra actions, multiplied HP, roll bonuses or hidden immunity. Such an effect exists only when explicitly included in the stat block.
275: Vaelor must not strengthen a boss during an encounter to make combat last longer. If a clever plan resolves the boss quickly, that outcome stands.
276: Completely overcoming a boss grants the same base XP whether it was defeated in combat, captured, outwitted, persuaded, driven away or otherwise genuinely resolved.
